title: Bloomberg Harvard Visiting Scholars Program 2026: Visiting Research Opportunity at Harvard University for Urban Problem-Solving and City Leadership
summary: The Bloomberg Harvard Visiting Scholars Program is inviting applications from researchers whose work aligns with the mission of the Bloomberg Center for Cities at Harvard University . The program supports rigorous, policy-relevant research focused on urban problem-solving and city leadership , with the aim of strengthening both academic scholarship and practical approaches to challenges facing cities. Selected applicants will be appointed as Bloomberg Harvard Visiting Scholars and will have the opportunity to spend either one semester or one full academic year in residence at the Bloomberg Center for Cities at Harvard University. The program is designed to provide scholars with protected time to advance a specific research project while also participating in the intellectual community of the Center and contributing to selected academic activities. Application Deadline: October 28, 2026 About the Bloomberg Harvard Visiting Scholars Program The Bloomberg Harvard Visiting Scholars Program is a new visiting scholar initiative of the Bloomberg Center for Cities at Harvard University . The program seeks to build a lasting and collaborative community of researchers whose work can contribute to the practice of urban problem-solving and city leadership . The program is particularly interested in research that can help cities and city leaders strengthen their capacity to: Drive performance Lead innovation Deliver results for residents Develop effective policies Strengthen organizational capabilities Use evidence and data effectively Collaborate across sectors The program therefore provides an opportunity for researchers to pursue rigorous research while engaging with a community focused on translating knowledge into better urban governance and outcomes. What Is the Bloomberg Center for Cities? The Bloomberg Center for Cities at Harvard University supports research and learning focused on helping cities and city leaders improve their ability to deliver results. The Center s interests extend across different dimensions of city leadership, management, organizational performance, innovation, evidence-based policymaking, data, artificial intelligence, and cross-sector collaboration. The Visiting Scholars Program is intended to contribute to this broader mission by bringing researchers into the Center s intellectual community for a dedicated period of research. Research Areas of Interest The Bloomberg Center for Cities supports research addressing significant questions related to urban problem-solving and city leadership . Areas of particular interest include, but are not limited to: 1. Mayoral Leadership and Management Strategies Research may examine how mayors and other city leaders manage organizations, implement priorities, lead change, and deliver results. Applicants working on leadership and management approaches within cities may find alignment with this area of interest. 2. High-Performing Staff and Teams Another area of interest is understanding the conditions that enable high-performing staff and teams . Research could examine organizational environments, management practices, leadership approaches, or other factors that contribute to effective public-sector teams. 3. Organizational Capabilities for Innovation The program is also interested in research examining how organizations develop the capabilities needed to innovate. This can include questions surrounding organizational structures, leadership, management, processes, and other conditions that support innovation in city government. 4. Evidence-Based Policy Solutions The Center is interested in evidence-based policy solutions and the capacity required to implement and deliver them. This creates an opportunity for researchers to examine not only which policies work, but also the institutional and organizational capabilities needed to put those policies into practice. 5. Data and Artificial Intelligence The use of data and artificial intelligence to strengthen decision-making is another area of particular interest. Researchers may explore how data and AI can support better decision-making in urban environments. 6. Cross-Sector Collaboration The program also highlights effective approaches to cross-sector collaboration . Research in this area may examine how governments, organizations, communities, and other actors can work together to address complex urban challenges. These areas are not presented as an exhaustive list. The broader focus is on research that advances understanding and practice in urban problem-solving and city leadership . Program Structure The Bloomberg Harvard Visiting Scholars Program is designed primarily to provide scholars with protected time for research . During their residency, selected scholars will focus primarily on advancing the research project described in their application. The residency can last for either: One semester , or One full academic year This flexibility allows selected scholars to participate in the program for a period that fits the scope of their research and individual circumstances. Research Focus During the Residency The central purpose of the residency is to give scholars dedicated time to develop their proposed research. The research project should be clearly defined in the application and should address a meaningful challenge related to urban problem-solving or city leadership. While research will be the primary focus, scholars will also be expected to contribute to the intellectual life of the Bloomberg Center for Cities through a limited number of structured activities. Activities and Expectations for Visiting Scholars In addition to their research, Bloomberg Harvard Visiting Scholars will participate in several activities during their residency. Research Seminar Scholars will be expected to host one research seminar per semester . The seminar should focus on the scholar s ongoing research or related themes. This provides an opportunity to share research with members of the Center s intellectual community and receive discussion and feedback. Student Study Group Scholars will also be expected to convene a student study group connected to their research . The study group will: Meet twice per month Include monthly office hours Facilitate discussion related to the scholar s research The study group is intended to facilitate discussion rather than function as formal classroom instruction. Harvard Community Event Each scholar will also organize one event , such as a talk or panel, that is open to the broader Harvard community. This provides another opportunity for scholars to share ideas and engage with the wider university community. Housing and Financial Support The program provides housing near Harvard University for participating scholars. In addition, financial assistance is available to help scholars dedicate sustained time to their proposed research project. Depending on an individual scholar s circumstances, financial support may be used to facilitate: Course buyout Other arrangements that allow the scholar to step back from regular academic obligations Dedicated time to focus on the proposed research The purpose of this support is to help selected scholars create sufficient protected time to advance their research during the residency. Visa Support The Bloomberg Center for Cities anticipates being able to sponsor visas for selected scholars , subject to: Institutional policies The individual scholar s circumstances International applicants should therefore consider the applicable visa and institutional requirements as part of the residency planning process. Who Can Apply? The program invites applications from researchers whose work aligns with the mission of the Bloomberg Center for Cities . Applicants may come from: Different disciplinary backgrounds Different career stages The program therefore does not restrict applicants to a single academic discipline, provided their research aligns with the Center s mission and interests. Academic Requirement Applicants must hold a: Doctoral degree (Ph.D. or comparable terminal research degree). This is a core eligibility requirement for the program. Current Academic or Research Appointment At the time of application, applicants must also hold a current faculty or research appointment at one of the following: A degree-granting university, or A recognized research institution Therefore, holding a doctoral degree alone is not sufficient. Applicants must also have a current qualifying faculty or research appointment when they apply. Research Proposal Requirements Applicants must submit a proposal describing the specific research project they intend to pursue during their residency . The proposal is a central part of the application and should clearly explain the research project and its relevance to urban problem-solving and city leadership. The proposal should address several important components. 1. Urban Problem or City Leadership Challenge Applicants should clearly identify the urban problem or city leadership challenge their research will address. The problem should be significant and connected to the broader mission of the Bloomberg Center for Cities. 2. Research Questions The proposal should explain the specific research question or questions that the project will examine. Applicants should also identify the theory or theories underpinning the work . 3. Research Design and Methodology Applicants should describe the research design and methodological approach they intend to use. This should demonstrate how the research questions will be investigated. 4. Significance for Research and Practice Applicants should explain why the project matters to both: The relevant research field, and The practice of urban problem-solving The program is particularly interested in work that can contribute not only to scholarship but also to real-world urban challenges. 5. Outputs and Potential Impact The proposal should also identify the types of outputs envisioned and the potential impact of the research. Applicants should therefore consider what their research could produce and how those outputs could contribute to scholarship and urban practice. Selection Process After applications are submitted, applicants may be invited to participate in an interview with members of a selection committee . Following the selection process, successful applicants will be formally appointed as Bloomberg Harvard Visiting Scholars . The selection process therefore considers both the submitted application and, where applicable, the interview stage. Selection Criteria Applications will be evaluated based on several key criteria. Clarity and Significance of the Research Problem The selection committee will consider how clearly the applicant identifies the research problem and the significance of the issue being studied. Strength of the Research Design The quality and strength of the proposed research design will also be considered. Applicants should clearly explain how their proposed methodology will address their research questions. Contribution to Scholarship and Practice The program will assess the potential contribution of the proposed research to: Academic scholarship The practice of urban problem-solving This reflects the program s emphasis on research that can have relevance beyond academia. Alignment With the Bloomberg Center for Cities Applications will also be evaluated based on their alignment with the mission and thematic interests of the Bloomberg Center for Cities . Applicants should therefore clearly demonstrate how their proposed research connects with the Center s focus on urban problem-solving and city leadership. Program Timeline The application timeline provided for the Bloomberg Harvard Visiting Scholars Program is: Stage Date Application Launch September 16, 2026 Application Deadline October 28, 2026 Notice of Selection February Applicants should complete and submit their application by October 28, 2026 . How to Prepare a Strong Application Prospective applicants should ensure that their application clearly connects their research with the program s focus. 1. Define the Urban Challenge Clearly Start by identifying the specific urban problem or city leadership challenge your research addresses. 2. Develop Clear Research Questions Make sure the research questions are specific and directly connected to the problem you identify. 3. Explain the Research Methodology Clearly describe how you intend to conduct the research and why the proposed methodology is appropriate. 4. Demonstrate Relevance to Urban Practice Explain how the research could contribute to practical urban problem-solving, rather than focusing exclusively on its academic contribution. 5. Show Alignment With the Center Connect your proposed project to relevant areas of interest at the Bloomberg Center for Cities, such as: City leadership Organizational performance Innovation Evidence-based policy Data and AI Cross-sector collaboration 6. Explain Potential Outputs Identify what you expect the research to produce and how those outputs could potentially contribute to research and practice. 7. Consider the Residency Commitment Applicants should consider whether a one-semester or full-year residency is appropriate for their research project and professional circumstances. Click HERE to read more. Why the Program May Be Valuable for Researchers The Bloomberg Harvard Visiting Scholars Program combines several components that can support researchers working on urban challenges. These include: Protected time dedicated primarily to research Residence at Harvard University s Bloomberg Center for Cities Access to an intellectual community focused on urban problem-solving Housing near Harvard University Financial assistance to support sustained research time Opportunities to engage with students Opportunities to organize research discussions and events Potential visa sponsorship for selected scholars, subject to institutional policies and individual circumstances Opportunities to connect academic research with practical urban leadership challenges The program s structure is particularly focused on creating an environment where scholars can advance a specific research project while contributing to a wider intellectual community. Application Deadline The Bloomberg Harvard Visiting Scholars Program application deadline is October 28, 2026 . Applications opened on September 16, 2026 . Prospective applicants should allow sufficient time to develop their research proposal, review their eligibility, and prepare the required application materials before the deadline. APPLY HERE Conclusion The Bloomberg Harvard Visiting Scholars Program offers researchers an opportunity to spend one semester or one full academic year in residence at Harvard University s Bloomberg Center for Cities , with protected time to advance a research project focused on urban problem-solving and city leadership. The program welcomes researchers from different disciplinary backgrounds and career stages, provided they meet the core eligibility requirements of holding a Ph.D. or comparable terminal research degree and a current faculty or research appointment at a degree-granting university or recognized research institution . Successful applicants will focus primarily on their proposed research while also contributing to the intellectual community through research seminars, student study groups, and a Harvard community event. Researchers whose work addresses issues such as mayoral leadership, high-performing teams, organizational innovation, evidence-based policy, data and artificial intelligence, or cross-sector collaboration may find particular alignment with the Center s areas of interest. With applications closing on October 28, 2026 , eligible researchers interested in advancing policy-relevant research on cities and urban leadership should review the program requirements and prepare their application before the deadline. title: Youth NTDs Fellowship Cohort 2 2026: 12-Week Hybrid Fellowship for Young Leaders in Tanzania and Kenya
summary: The Youth NTDs Fellowship Cohort 2 is now inviting applications from young people aged 18 to 35 who are interested in or have experience in neglected tropical diseases (NTDs), One Health, community engagement, advocacy, health systems, and related areas . Organized by One Health Society (OHS), Tanzania , in partnership with the Global Alliance for NTDs Elimination (GANE), Kenya , the 12-week hybrid fellowship is designed to equip young leaders with practical knowledge, skills, mentorship, and opportunities to contribute to NTD elimination efforts. The fellowship brings together young people who are interested in addressing NTD-related challenges and strengthening community and health-system responses. Participants will receive guidance from expert mentors and work collaboratively on team-based capstone projects. Application Deadline: 25 September 2026 About the Youth NTDs Fellowship Cohort 2 The Youth NTDs Fellowship is a 12-week hybrid leadership and capacity-building programme focused on preparing young people to contribute meaningfully to efforts to eliminate neglected tropical diseases. The programme combines learning, mentorship, practical skill development, community-focused approaches, and collaborative project work. For Cohort 2, participants will have the opportunity to develop practical skills across several interconnected areas, including: One Health NTD elimination Community engagement Advocacy Health systems integration Solution development Rather than focusing only on theoretical knowledge, the fellowship is structured to support young people in developing practical skills that can be applied to real-world NTD and One Health challenges. The programme also provides participants with access to expert mentors and opportunities to work with other young leaders through team-based capstone projects . What Are Neglected Tropical Diseases? Neglected tropical diseases, commonly referred to as NTDs , are a group of diseases that disproportionately affect populations and communities facing conditions such as poverty and limited access to healthcare and other essential services. Addressing NTDs requires more than medical interventions alone. Community participation, health-system strengthening, advocacy, awareness, prevention, and collaboration across different sectors can all contribute to effective disease elimination efforts. This is why the Youth NTDs Fellowship incorporates a One Health approach , connecting human health with broader community and health-system considerations. What Will the Fellowship Focus On? The Youth NTDs Fellowship Cohort 2 is designed around several major areas of learning and practical development. 1. One Health Participants will develop an understanding of the One Health approach , which recognizes the interconnected nature of health and the importance of collaboration across different sectors and disciplines. This perspective can help young leaders understand NTD challenges within their wider community and health-system context. 2. NTD Elimination The fellowship focuses specifically on neglected tropical disease elimination , helping participants strengthen their understanding of the challenges and approaches associated with NTD control and elimination. Participants with existing experience or interest in NTDs can use the fellowship as an opportunity to deepen their engagement in this area. 3. Community Engagement Community involvement is an important part of addressing NTD-related challenges. The fellowship will equip young leaders with practical skills related to community engagement , helping them consider how communities can be meaningfully involved in health initiatives and solutions. 4. Advocacy Participants will also develop skills in advocacy , enabling them to better understand how young people and community actors can contribute to raising awareness and supporting action around NTD-related issues. 5. Health Systems Integration The programme also focuses on health systems integration , helping fellows understand how NTD-related interventions and solutions can connect with broader health systems. This provides an opportunity for participants to consider NTD elimination from a wider health-system perspective rather than as an isolated issue. 6. Solution Development A further focus of the fellowship is solution development . Through collaborative activities and capstone projects, fellows will have an opportunity to apply their learning to practical challenges and work together to develop potential solutions. Expert Mentorship and Capstone Projects One of the key components of the fellowship is the combination of expert mentorship and team-based capstone projects . Participants will be supported by expert mentors throughout the fellowship while working with other fellows on collaborative projects. The capstone component provides an opportunity to move beyond learning and apply skills to practical challenges related to NTDs, One Health, community engagement, advocacy, health systems integration, or solution development. Working in teams can also allow participants to learn from peers with different experiences and perspectives. Fellowship Duration and Time Commitment The Youth NTDs Fellowship Cohort 2 will run for 12 weeks . The fellowship is structured as a hybrid programme , meaning participants will engage through a combination of formats as determined by the programme organizers. Applicants should be prepared to commit approximately: 6–8 hours per week for 12 weeks. This means applicants should consider their existing academic, professional, community, or other commitments before applying and ensure that they can dedicate the required time throughout the fellowship. Who Should Apply? The fellowship is intended for young people aged 18–35 from Tanzania and Kenya who have an interest or experience in areas related to: Neglected tropical diseases One Health Public health Community engagement Health advocacy Health systems Related fields Applicants do not necessarily need to be established NTD specialists. The opportunity is aimed at young people who have an interest or experience in NTDs, One Health, or related fields and want to strengthen their skills and contribution in these areas. Applicants Particularly Encouraged to Apply The organizers particularly encourage applications from several groups, including: Young People from NTD-Endemic Communities Young people who come from communities affected by NTDs are especially encouraged to apply. Their community experience can provide valuable perspectives on the challenges associated with NTDs and potential approaches to addressing them. People With Lived Experience of NTDs People with lived experience of neglected tropical diseases are also especially encouraged to apply. Their direct experiences can contribute important perspectives to discussions around NTD elimination and community-focused solutions. People With Disabilities The fellowship particularly encourages applications from people with disabilities . Women Women are specifically encouraged to apply to the fellowship. Community Actors Young community actors with an interest or experience in NTDs, One Health, or related fields are also encouraged to apply. Why Participate in the Youth NTDs Fellowship? The fellowship offers young participants an opportunity to strengthen practical skills while engaging with other young leaders working around NTD and One Health-related issues. Key areas of development include: Practical One Health skills Understanding of NTD elimination Community engagement approaches Advocacy skills Health systems integration Solution development Team-based project experience Mentorship from experts Exposure to other young people working in related areas The combination of structured learning, mentorship, and a capstone project can provide participants with an opportunity to connect knowledge with practical application. Application Deadline The application deadline for the Youth NTDs Fellowship Cohort 2 is: 25 September 2026 Applicants should ensure that they submit their application by the stated deadline. Because the deadline is approaching, eligible young people interested in the programme should review the requirements and prepare their application information in advance. Important Information for Applicants Applicants are asked to provide accurate information in the application form. According to the fellowship announcement, the information provided will be used for purposes including: Selection Fellowship planning Mentorship Monitoring, Evaluation and Learning (MEL) Related programme purposes Applicants should therefore ensure that the information they provide is complete and accurate. APPLY HERE How to Prepare for the Fellowship Application Before applying, prospective fellows should consider the following: Confirm your age eligibility Applicants should be between 18 and 35 years old. Confirm your country eligibility The fellowship is intended for young people from Tanzania and Kenya. Review your relevant experience or interest Consider your experience or interest in NTDs, One Health, public health, community engagement, advocacy, health systems, or related fields. Consider your availability The programme requires approximately 6–8 hours per week over 12 weeks. Reflect on your community experience Applicants can consider how their experiences, community involvement, or professional interests connect with NTDs and One Health. Provide accurate information Ensure that all information submitted through the application form is truthful and accurate. Submit before the deadline The deadline is 25 September 2026 . Conclusion The Youth NTDs Fellowship Cohort 2 provides young people from Tanzania and Kenya with a structured 12-week opportunity to strengthen their knowledge and practical skills in One Health, neglected tropical disease elimination, community engagement, advocacy, health systems integration, and solution development . Through expert mentorship and team-based capstone projects, the fellowship is designed to connect young leaders with practical experiences and collaborative learning. Young people aged 18–35 with an interest or experience in NTDs, One Health, or related fields are encouraged to consider applying. The organizers particularly encourage applications from NTD-endemic communities, people with lived experience of NTDs and/or disability, women, and community actors . With a commitment of 6–8 hours per week for 12 weeks , applicants should ensure they have sufficient availability to participate fully. Application Deadline: 25 September 2026 Click HERE for more fellowship opportunities. title: GFF × CIVIC VOICES Call for Proposals 2026: Up to USD 3.35 Million in Grants for African Civil Society and Youth-Led Organizations
summary: The GFF × CIVIC VOICES Call for Proposals 2026 is providing a major funding opportunity for local civil society organizations (CSOs), youth-led organizations, and community-based organizations working to strengthen civic engagement, advocacy, and domestic resource mobilization for the health and nutrition of women, children, and adolescents across Africa. Through the VOICES (Voices Organizing for Inclusive Civic Engagement and Sustainability) consortium, selected organizations can receive grants of up to 18 months , alongside advocacy training, budget analysis technical assistance, and mentorship. A total of up to USD 3,350,000 will be awarded across up to 22 African countries , making this an important opportunity for organizations seeking resources to strengthen their advocacy, coalition-building, youth leadership, and engagement in health financing. GFF × CIVIC VOICES Call for Proposals 2026 The initiative is part of the World Bank Group’s GFF × CIVIC partnership , a joint initiative involving the Global Financing Facility for Women, Children and Adolescents (GFF) and CIVIC: The Civil Society and Social Innovation Alliance . The partnership recognizes that civil society and youth-led organizations play an important role in improving health and nutrition outcomes for women, children, and adolescents. However, organizations can face barriers that limit their ability to participate effectively in policymaking, advocacy, financing discussions, and other decision-making processes. The VOICES consortium seeks to address some of these barriers by supporting local organizations to strengthen their capacity and influence. The consortium is led by PATH , in partnership with the African Institute for Development Policy (AFIDEP) and the Organisation of African Youth (OAY) . Together, these organizations operate as VOICES—Voices Organizing for Inclusive Civic Engagement and Sustainability . What Is the GFF × CIVIC VOICES Initiative? The initiative focuses on strengthening civil society engagement, coalition-building, and youth leadership around domestic resource mobilization for women s, children s, and adolescent health and nutrition . Domestic resource mobilization refers broadly to efforts to generate and allocate resources within countries to support important public priorities, including healthcare. By supporting civil society and youth-led organizations, the initiative aims to strengthen their ability to participate in discussions and advocacy around health financing and resource allocation. The funding opportunity therefore goes beyond providing financial resources. Selected organizations will also receive capacity-building and technical support intended to strengthen their advocacy work. Funding Available The VOICES consortium will provide: Up to USD 3,350,000 in total financial support. Funding across up to 22 African countries . Grants lasting up to 18 months . Advocacy training. Budget analysis technical assistance. Mentorship. The source specifies that funding will be distributed across eligible organizations and partnerships in the participating African countries. Who Can Apply? The funding opportunity is intended for local civil society organizations, youth-led organizations, and/or community-based organizations . An important requirement is that applications must involve a partnership rather than a single organization applying independently. Each partnership must include: At least 2 organizations . No more than 3 organizations . At least 1 youth-led organization . This partnership structure is designed to encourage collaboration between organizations and strengthen coalition-building. Organizations considering an application should therefore identify suitable local partners and ensure that the proposed partnership meets the required composition. Focus on Youth Leadership Youth leadership is an important component of the GFF × CIVIC VOICES opportunity. Every partnership must include at least one youth-led organization . This means youth-led organizations are not simply potential participants in the initiative; their inclusion is an explicit requirement of the partnership structure. The opportunity connects youth leadership with broader civil society engagement around women s, children s, and adolescent health and nutrition. This creates opportunities for youth-led organizations to participate in advocacy, coalition-building, domestic resource mobilization discussions, and efforts to improve civic engagement. What Will Selected Organizations Receive? Successful applicants will receive financial support for projects that align with the objectives of the funding opportunity. In addition to the grants, the program provides several forms of capacity development. 1. Financial Support The overall funding pool is worth up to USD 3.35 million across up to 22 African countries. Individual grant amounts should be determined according to the official call documentation and application requirements. 2. Advocacy Training Selected organizations will have access to advocacy training designed to strengthen their ability to engage in policy and advocacy processes. This can support organizations seeking to increase their effectiveness when engaging policymakers, communities, stakeholders, and other relevant actors. 3. Budget Analysis Technical Assistance The program also provides budget analysis technical assistance . This is particularly relevant to the initiative s focus on domestic resource mobilization, as organizations can strengthen their ability to understand and engage with health-related budgets and financing discussions. 4. Mentorship Selected organizations will also receive mentorship , providing additional support as they implement their work and strengthen their organizational and advocacy capacity. Key Areas of Focus The funding opportunity is particularly connected to three major areas: Civil Society Engagement The initiative seeks to strengthen the participation and influence of civil society organizations in health and nutrition-related processes. Coalition-Building Partnerships are central to the opportunity. The requirement for two to three organizations encourages organizations to work together and develop stronger collaborative approaches. Youth Leadership Youth-led organizations must be part of every partnership, placing youth leadership at the center of the initiative. These areas are connected to the broader goal of strengthening advocacy around domestic resource mobilization for women s, children s, and adolescent health and nutrition . Geographic Scope The funding opportunity will support organizations in up to 22 African countries . The source provided with this opportunity includes a VOICES eligible countries graphic , but the pasted information does not provide the country names in text. Applicants should therefore consult the official call documents and eligibility materials to confirm whether their country is included before preparing an application. Grant Duration Successful partnerships can receive grants lasting up to 18 months . This provides organizations with a substantial period in which to implement activities, strengthen partnerships, conduct advocacy, and work toward the objectives outlined in their proposals. Applicants should carefully review the official call documentation for the specific expectations concerning project duration, activities, budgets, and implementation. Application Deadline The application deadline is: Wednesday, October 7, 2026, at 23:59 East Africa Time (EAT). Organizations interested in applying should allow sufficient time to develop their partnership, prepare the technical proposal, review the application requirements, and submit all required materials before the deadline. How to Apply Applicants should review the official GFF × CIVIC VOICES Call for Proposals and accompanying application materials before preparing their submission. The available resources include: Call for Proposals: VOICES Call for Proposals PDF Technical Proposal Submission Template: VOICES Technical Proposal Submission Template Frequently Asked Questions: VOICES Frequently Asked Questions Applicants can also consult the official GFF × CIVIC VOICES funding opportunity resources for additional information, including submission details and launch event materials. GFF × CIVIC VOICES Funding Opportunity Resources Questions and Concerns The VOICES Consortium provides an email channel for questions and concerns relating to the opportunity. Applicants can contact: voices@path.org The consortium also provides an anonymous grievance mechanism through PATH s secure reporting system for those who wish to submit a grievance anonymously. How Organizations Can Prepare Organizations interested in this funding opportunity should consider several practical steps before submitting an application. Build the Right Partnership Because every application must involve 2–3 organizations and include at least one youth-led organization , applicants should establish their partnership early. Review the Official Call Carefully The official call documents should be used to confirm detailed eligibility requirements, country eligibility, proposal requirements, funding rules, and submission procedures. Develop a Clear Project Concept A strong proposal should clearly explain what the partnership intends to accomplish and how the proposed activities connect with the objectives of the VOICES initiative. Demonstrate Collaboration Since coalition-building is one of the initiative s core areas, applicants should clearly explain the roles and contributions of each organization within the partnership. Consider Youth Leadership At least one youth-led organization must be included. Applicants should therefore ensure that youth leadership is meaningfully reflected in the partnership rather than treating the youth-led organization as a purely formal participant. Prepare Early With the deadline set for October 7, 2026 , organizations should avoid waiting until the final days to prepare and submit their proposal. Learn more HERE Why This Funding Opportunity Matters The GFF × CIVIC VOICES Call for Proposals brings together funding, advocacy capacity-building, technical assistance, mentorship, civil society engagement, and youth leadership . For eligible African organizations, the opportunity provides a mechanism to strengthen collaborative advocacy around domestic resource mobilization for women s, children s, and adolescent health and nutrition. The partnership model also encourages organizations to work collectively rather than operating in isolation, while the mandatory participation of a youth-led organization gives young people and youth-led organizations an explicit role within the supported partnerships. Conclusion The GFF × CIVIC VOICES Call for Proposals 2026 offers up to USD 3.35 million in financial support across up to 22 African countries for partnerships involving local civil society, youth-led, and/or community-based organizations. Eligible partnerships must consist of 2–3 organizations , with at least one youth-led organization , and successful applicants can receive grants of up to 18 months , together with advocacy training, budget analysis technical assistance, and mentorship. Organizations interested in applying should review the official call documentation and supporting resources carefully, confirm their eligibility and country participation, develop the required partnership, and submit their application before 7 October 2026 at 23:59 East Africa Time. title: British Red Cross Youth Engagement & Early Careers Internship 2026: Paid London Opportunity for Young People
summary: The British Red Cross Youth Engagement Early Careers Internship 2026 offers young people an opportunity to gain practical workplace experience while contributing to projects designed to improve opportunities, career development and resilience for young people. Based in London , with hybrid working between home and the British Red Cross offices, this six-month internship provides hands-on experience in youth engagement, early careers, recruitment data, project support and resource development. The internship offers a salary of £24,479 per annum , with an additional Inner London Weighting (ILW) of £3,344 pro rata for eligible employees residing and working in London. The position is full-time at 35 hours per week , Monday to Friday, and is scheduled to run from November 2026 to May 2027 . Applications are currently open, and interested candidates should submit their applications before the 27 September 2026 deadline . British Red Cross Youth Engagement Early Careers Internship 2026 Overview The internship is designed for young people who want to develop their professional experience while helping create meaningful opportunities for other young people. As a Youth Engagement Early Careers Intern, the successful candidate will work alongside colleagues across the British Red Cross and contribute to projects focused on improving young people s access to opportunities. The role combines practical workplace experience with youth-focused project work. Interns will have opportunities to engage directly with young people, collect feedback and insights, support events and workshops, analyse recruitment information and help develop resources related to youth engagement and early careers. Key Details Organisation: British Red Cross Position: Youth Engagement Early Careers Intern Location: London, United Kingdom Working arrangement: Hybrid, between home and the London offices Office location: EC2Y 9AL Salary: £24,479 per annum London weighting: £3,344 pro rata, where applicable Working hours: 35 hours per week Working days: Monday to Friday Contract: Fixed-term Duration: Six months Expected period: November 2026 to May 2027 Application deadline: 27 September 2026 at 23:59 Assessment Centre: Expected to take place in London during the week commencing 5 October 2026 About the Youth Engagement Early Careers Internship The internship focuses on helping young people access opportunities, develop confidence and strengthen their career resilience. The successful intern will contribute to work that seeks to understand the experiences and needs of young people and identify ways to make paid opportunities more accessible and inclusive. Rather than being limited to administrative tasks, the position involves several areas of practical project work, including youth engagement, events, data analysis, research, resource development and communication. The role can therefore provide experience across different areas of organisational work while maintaining a strong focus on young people and early-career development. What Will a Youth Engagement Early Careers Intern Do? The intern will support several activities throughout the placement. 1. Engage With Young People A key responsibility will be engaging with young people and gathering their feedback. The information collected through these interactions can help the British Red Cross understand young people s experiences and use those insights to shape projects, resources and opportunities. This may give the intern experience in: Youth engagement Gathering feedback Listening to young people s perspectives Understanding user experiences Supporting project development Contributing to improvements in youth-focused opportunities The role therefore places young people s experiences at the centre of some of the work the intern will support. 2. Support Youth Engagement Events and Workshops The intern will also help with youth engagement events, workshops and activities . This could provide practical experience in supporting activities that involve groups of young people and colleagues from across the organisation. Through this work, the intern can develop skills in areas such as organisation, communication, event support and relationship building. 3. Analyse Recruitment Data Another important part of the position involves analysing recruitment data relating to young people. The purpose is to help identify ways of improving access to paid opportunities. This gives the intern exposure to the relationship between data and organisational decision-making. Instead of simply collecting information, the role involves looking at what the information can reveal and considering how it could inform improvements. 4. Develop Resources and Case Studies The intern will contribute to the development of: Resources Case studies Insights Youth engagement materials Career resilience materials Early-career opportunity resources This aspect of the role can help the successful candidate develop experience in research, writing, communication and turning information into useful resources. Skills and Qualities Required The British Red Cross is looking for candidates who demonstrate an interest in helping young people and contributing to positive opportunities. Genuine Interest in Supporting Young People Applicants should have a genuine interest in supporting young people and helping create positive opportunities for others. title: The Nature Conservancy Strategic Content and Storytelling Manager – Africa Region 2026: Full-Time Communications Role Across Six African Countries
summary: The Nature Conservancy is recruiting a Strategic Content and Storytelling Manager – Africa Region , a senior full-time communications and editorial role for an experienced storyteller who can turn complex conservation, scientific and community-based work into compelling narratives for donors, partners, policymakers and wider public audiences. The position is part of The Nature Conservancy’s Africa Marketing and Communications team and is designed for an experienced communications professional who combines strong writing and editing ability with strategic content planning, field reporting, multimedia production, audience engagement and editorial leadership. The role may be based in a country where The Nature Conservancy has an office in Kenya, Tanzania, Gabon, Zambia, South Africa or Angola . Importantly, the organization states that it is not offering employment visas or immigration assistance for this position , apart from fulfilling normal local employment requirements. This is a particularly relevant opportunity for professionals with backgrounds in journalism, communications, media, editorial publishing, conservation communications, nonprofit storytelling, sustainability, development communications or multimedia content development. Job requisition ID: JR103833 Employment type: Full-time Application deadline: The Nature Conservancy does not publish a fixed closing date in the vacancy. Applications are reviewed on a rolling basis, and the organization states that the position may be removed once a strong candidate pool has been identified. Candidates are therefore encouraged to apply as early as possible. About the Strategic Content and Storytelling Manager – Africa Region Role The Strategic Content and Storytelling Manager will be responsible for shaping and driving The Nature Conservancy Africa Region’s content vision, editorial strategy and storytelling agenda . The position is not simply a writing or social-media role. It is a senior content leadership position responsible for creating a coherent storytelling strategy for conservation work across Africa. The successful candidate will help The Nature Conservancy communicate: Conservation impact Community experiences Partner contributions Scientific work Donor-supported outcomes Regional priorities Conservation challenges Organizational achievements The role is intended to help TNC develop narratives that strengthen relationships with supporters, elevate community and partner voices, support philanthropic engagement and increase public understanding of conservation work across Africa. What Will the Strategic Content and Storytelling Manager Do? The position covers five major areas: Content strategy and editorial leadership Story development and narrative creation Multimedia storytelling and production Audience engagement and content performance Internal collaboration and editorial consulting The successful candidate will manage stories through the entire content-development process, from identifying an idea in the field to producing, publishing and evaluating the final content. 1. Lead The Nature Conservancy’s Africa Content Strategy A major responsibility will be developing and owning the Africa region’s overall content and storytelling strategy. The manager will align storytelling with: Regional priorities Conservation objectives Philanthropic engagement goals Organizational brand standards The role also involves building an annual editorial roadmap that identifies: Priority themes Major narratives Target audiences Storytelling opportunities Content priorities across Africa The successful candidate will ensure that TNC maintains a consistent pipeline of strong stories throughout the year rather than producing content only in response to individual events or requests. Establish Editorial Standards The manager will help define the overall editorial identity of TNC Africa. This includes developing and maintaining standards relating to: Voice Tone Editorial quality Narrative structure Storytelling frameworks Content governance The successful candidate will also advise senior leaders and programme teams on how storytelling can better communicate conservation impact and engage priority audiences. This means the position requires both creative skills and strategic judgment. The manager must be able to answer questions such as: Which stories should TNC prioritize? Which audiences should a story target? What format would communicate it most effectively? Which voices should be included? How can complex science be made understandable without oversimplifying it? How should donor-supported impact be communicated authentically? 2. Serve as the Lead Storyteller for TNC Africa The vacancy describes the successful candidate as the lead storyteller, writer and editor for the Africa region . This is one of the central features of the position. The manager will identify, research and develop stories involving: Landscapes Communities Indigenous Peoples Conservation practitioners Scientists Donors Partners TNC staff The objective is to uncover meaningful stories from TNC’s work and communicate them to different audiences in ways that are credible, engaging and evidence-based. Translate Complex Science Into Accessible Stories A key requirement is the ability to take complicated scientific, technical and conservation information and transform it into clear narratives. This may involve converting: Scientific research Conservation data Technical reports Monitoring findings Environmental analysis Community conservation work into content that non-specialist audiences can understand. This is particularly important because The Nature Conservancy is a science-based organization, while many of the audiences consuming its content may not have technical conservation backgrounds. Produce Multiple Types of Written Content The position will create and edit a wide variety of materials, including: Feature stories Long-form articles Case studies Donor stories Scripts Blogs Impact reports Applicants should therefore demonstrate more than short-form communications experience. A strong candidate should ideally have a portfolio showing an ability to work across different editorial styles and audiences. Conduct Interviews and Field Reporting The role requires direct story gathering. The manager will conduct interviews and gather firsthand information from people involved in conservation work. That could include conversations with: Community leaders Local residents Scientists Conservation staff Government counterparts NGO partners Indigenous representatives Donors The role therefore requires strong interviewing ability and the judgment to represent people accurately and ethically. Ethical and Inclusive Storytelling The Nature Conservancy specifically states that its content should reflect: Diverse voices Local perspectives Ethical storytelling practices This is particularly important in conservation communications, where organizations may tell stories about communities, traditional knowledge, land, livelihoods and natural resources. The successful candidate should understand that communities are not merely subjects of stories. Their perspectives, agency and experiences should be represented appropriately. 3. Lead Multimedia Storytelling The position extends far beyond writing. The Strategic Content and Storytelling Manager will lead multimedia projects involving: Video Photography Audio Digital storytelling Other creative formats The role may therefore suit candidates who have experience in journalism, documentary storytelling, multimedia production or creative editorial development. Work With Photographers, Videographers and Designers The manager will collaborate with external and internal creative professionals, including: Photographers Videographers Designers Editors Production partners Creative agencies Responsibilities will include developing: Creative briefs Storytelling concepts Production plans Editorial objectives The manager will also oversee production workflows to make sure finished material remains consistent with TNC’s broader editorial strategy. Field Travel Is Part of the Job The position requires travel to field locations for: Reporting Interviews Story gathering Content production The vacancy lists approximately: 20% travel. This is therefore not a purely desk-based editorial position. Candidates should be comfortable travelling to conservation landscapes and working directly with teams, communities and partners. Big 5 Irreplaceable Landscapes Storytelling The vacancy specifically mentions helping bring The Nature Conservancy’s Big 5 Irreplaceable Landscapes story to life. The communications team wants the successful candidate to help connect donors and other audiences with: People Places Conservation results Outcomes made possible by philanthropic support This illustrates the close relationship between storytelling and fundraising within the position. The role is expected to communicate not only what conservation teams are doing but why the work matters and what donor support enables. Main Publishing Platforms The primary platform for storytelling will be: Nature.org However, the vacancy also identifies a range of other formats, including: Video productions Blogs Podcasts Photo stories Multimedia content A successful candidate should therefore understand how stories need to be adapted for different channels rather than simply republishing identical content everywhere. 4. Measure Content Performance The role has a significant analytical component. The successful candidate will monitor content performance using: Audience insights Analytics Engagement metrics Audience behavior The manager will evaluate how stories perform across different channels and use those findings to improve future editorial decisions. This means applicants should be comfortable with the idea that content success is measurable. Strong storytelling remains central, but decisions should also be informed by evidence about: What audiences engage with What content reaches priority groups Which formats perform effectively Which stories support donor engagement Which narratives improve visibility Storytelling and Donor Engagement The role will also assess whether storytelling initiatives support: Donor engagement Partnership development Organizational visibility This is an important distinction. The position is not intended solely to generate public-facing media attention. Stories must also support relationships with: Philanthropic partners Donors Strategic partners Institutional stakeholders Candidates with experience in nonprofit, development or philanthropic communications may therefore be particularly relevant. 5. Work Across TNC Teams The manager will collaborate extensively throughout The Nature Conservancy. Internal partners may include teams working in: Philanthropy Conservation Science Policy Country programmes Digital communications The role therefore requires someone who can work across professional disciplines. A conservation scientist may think differently from a fundraising professional. A country director may have different priorities from a digital communications specialist. The storytelling manager must be capable of understanding these different perspectives and turning them into a coherent content strategy. Provide Editorial Guidance to Colleagues The successful candidate will also serve as an internal storytelling expert. Responsibilities include: Advising colleagues Editing internally produced content Strengthening partner content Providing storytelling guidance Sharing best practices The manager will therefore influence content produced by others in addition to producing stories personally. Elevate African Stories Globally Another responsibility is building networks and collaborations that help Africa-region stories reach wider global audiences. This could involve connecting regional communications priorities with TNC’s wider international channels. The successful candidate should therefore be able to think simultaneously at: Local level Country level Regional Africa level Global organizational level Minimum Qualifications The formal qualifications section identifies the following core requirement: Bachelor’s degree in Journalism, Communications, Media Studies, English or a related field, plus at least seven years of related experience, or an equivalent combination of education and experience. Applicants also need: Exceptional writing skills Strong editing ability Interviewing skills Narrative-development expertise Experience developing content strategies Experience managing editorial pipelines Experience working across written, digital, visual and multimedia formats Preferred Level of Experience The vacancy separately lists: Eight or more years of professional experience in areas such as: Content strategy Editorial leadership Journalism Storytelling Publishing Multimedia content development as a desired qualification. The distinction is worth noting: The basic qualification refers to a bachelor s degree plus a minimum seven years of related experience , or equivalent. The desired profile highlights 8+ years . Candidates with seven years should not automatically rule themselves out if they otherwise meet the stated minimum requirements. Preferred Professional Backgrounds TNC particularly values candidates with experience in sectors including: Conservation Environment Development Sustainability Nonprofit organizations Relevant professional backgrounds may therefore include: Conservation communications Development communications Environmental journalism NGO communications Science journalism Sustainability communications Documentary storytelling Editorial publishing Donor communications Journalism and Documentary Experience A background in: Journalism Documentary storytelling Editorial publishing is specifically identified as desirable. This is notable because the position blends institutional communications with journalistic storytelling practices. TNC appears to be seeking someone who understands how to identify, investigate and structure a genuine story rather than simply produce corporate messaging. Experience Writing for Donors and Partners Candidates with experience creating content for: Donors Philanthropic audiences Partnerships are particularly relevant. This requires a particular type of storytelling. Donor stories need to demonstrate: Impact Evidence Human relevance Credibility Connection between support and results without becoming overly promotional or losing the perspectives of communities involved. Digital Analytics Experience TNC also values knowledge of: Digital content metrics Audience analytics Engagement strategies Applicants should therefore mention relevant experience with: Website analytics Content-performance measurement Audience segmentation Engagement metrics Digital publishing tools where applicable. Experience Across African Countries The desired qualifications include: Experience working across multiple African countries and cultures. This makes regional experience particularly valuable. The role requires sensitivity to the fact that Africa is not one homogeneous communications environment. Stories from Kenya, Gabon, Angola, Tanzania, Zambia or South Africa may involve different: Languages Cultural contexts Conservation issues Political environments Community relationships Media landscapes Candidates should demonstrate cultural awareness and an ability to adapt storytelling appropriately. Ethical Storytelling and Representation TNC specifically seeks candidates with: A strong understanding of ethical storytelling, representation and inclusive narrative practices. This is likely to be particularly important when working with: Indigenous Peoples Rural communities Conservation-affected communities Local partners Traditional knowledge holders Applicants should be prepared to demonstrate how they approach issues such as: Consent Representation Agency Attribution Dignity Context Power dynamics in storytelling. Portfolio Requirement A strong portfolio is an important part of the desired profile. TNC wants evidence demonstrating: Impactful storytelling Editorial leadership High-quality written work Multimedia capability Strategic content development Candidates should therefore select portfolio material strategically. A strong portfolio might show different formats rather than several very similar pieces. Field Reporting Experience Candidates should ideally have experience gathering stories through: Direct field reporting Stakeholder interviews This requirement reinforces the practical nature of the role. The successful candidate will not simply wait for programme teams to submit material. They will actively go into the field to identify and report stories. Project Management Skills The job requires excellent project-management capability. The successful candidate should be comfortable managing multiple content projects at the same time. This may involve simultaneously coordinating: Writers Photographers Videographers Editors Country teams Programme staff External agencies Production deadlines Strong organizational skills will therefore be essential. Collaboration Across Cultures and Time Zones Excellent relationship-building skills are also required. Candidates should be able to collaborate across: Cultures Functions Locations Time zones Because TNC is a global organization, regional communications work may involve collaboration both within Africa and with colleagues elsewhere. Language Requirement Applicants must be fluent in: Written and spoken English. The listing does not state a formal requirement for French, Portuguese or other African languages. Additional languages may nevertheless be professionally useful given the role s regional scope, but they should not be presented as mandatory unless TNC states otherwise. Travel Requirement The role involves approximately: 20% travel. Travel is likely to support: Field reporting Interviews Conservation storytelling Photography and video production Meetings with partners and teams Candidates should therefore be willing and able to travel as part of their regular responsibilities. Driver’s Licence Requirement The position requires a: Valid driver s licence. Employees must also comply with TNC s Auto Safety Program. Employment is contingent on completing a Vehicle Use Agreement, which may include review of the applicant s motor vehicle record. Applicants should not overlook this requirement. Where Can the Position Be Based? The vacancy lists the role across TNC s offices in: Kenya Tanzania Gabon Zambia South Africa Angola The job listing specifically displays locations including Kenya, Luanda in Angola, Mumbwa in Zambia, Tanzania and Gabon, while the role description confirms all six eligible office countries. The vacancy does not present the role as open for fully remote employment from any African country. Candidates should therefore understand that they need to be employable in one of the identified TNC office countries. Visa Sponsorship This is one of the most important eligibility considerations. The Nature Conservancy states: No employment visas or assistance are being offered for this position, except for local labour employment requirements. Therefore, candidates should generally already possess the legal right or practical ability to be employed locally in one of the eligible countries. International applicants who would require employer-sponsored relocation or a new work visa should not assume that sponsorship will be available. Salary The vacancy includes a “Salary Information” heading but does not provide a salary figure in the material published with the listing. Applicants should therefore not rely on unofficial salary estimates. Compensation may vary according to: Country Local employment market TNC compensation frameworks Candidate experience Benefits The Nature Conservancy states that it provides competitive benefits packages tailored to the individual countries where it operates. Depending on country and employment arrangements, benefits may include : Healthcare benefits Retirement benefits Parental leave Paid time off Life insurance Disability coverage Employee assistance programme Other wellbeing benefits The word “may” is important because benefits differ between countries. The vacancy also emphasizes a flexible work environment intended to support employee health and wellbeing. About The Nature Conservancy The Nature Conservancy is a global environmental nonprofit whose mission is: “To conserve the lands and waters on which all life depends.” Founded in 1951 in the United States, the organization has developed into a major international conservation organization. According to the vacancy, TNC has: More than one million members More than 400 scientists Conservation impact across 79 countries and territories Its work is science-based and focuses on developing practical responses to environmental and conservation challenges. TNC s Workplace Approach The organization says it aims to create an inclusive working environment in which colleagues from different backgrounds feel that their contributions are valued. TNC also notes that applicants may bring valuable skills and experience from outside conventional job requirements and encourages potentially relevant candidates to apply. Equal Opportunity Statement The Nature Conservancy describes itself as an Equal Opportunity Employer. Its recruitment commitment includes applicants across differences in: Culture Race Colour Religion Sex National or regional origin Age Disability Sexual orientation Gender identity Military status Protected veteran status Other legally protected categories The organization also provides reasonable accommodation during the recruitment process for qualified applicants with disabilities. Is There a Fixed Application Deadline? No fixed calendar deadline is stated in the vacancy. Instead, TNC says it uses a: Rolling interview process. Applications may be reviewed in the order they are received. Once the organization identifies a sufficiently strong candidate pool, the vacancy may be removed. For that reason, interested candidates should apply as soon as possible rather than waiting for a nonexistent final deadline. How to Apply Applications should be submitted through The Nature Conservancy s official Workday careers system. Job requisition: JR103833 APPLY HERE How to Make Your Application Stronger Candidates applying for this position should pay particular attention to their portfolio and evidence of strategic editorial leadership . A competitive application should demonstrate several things at once. First, show that you are an excellent storyteller. Include examples where you transformed a complicated issue into compelling and understandable content. Second, demonstrate strategy. TNC is not simply hiring an experienced writer; it is hiring someone who can build and manage an editorial direction across an entire region. Third, show your ability to work with people. Examples involving interviews, field reporting, community voices or stakeholder engagement can be particularly relevant. Fourth, demonstrate multimedia capability. If you have produced or managed video, photography, podcasts, data stories or multimedia packages, make that visible. Finally, candidates with conservation, environmental, development, sustainability or nonprofit experience should make those connections explicit. Key Information at a Glance Position: Strategic Content and Storytelling Manager – Africa Region Organization: The Nature Conservancy Job ID: JR103833 Employment type: Full-time Region: Africa Potential duty countries: Kenya, Tanzania, Gabon, Zambia, South Africa and Angola Main field: Communications, content strategy, storytelling and conservation communications Minimum education/experience: Bachelor s degree in Journalism, Communications, Media Studies, English or related field plus at least seven years of relevant experience, or equivalent combination of education and experience Preferred professional experience: 8+ years Language: Fluent written and spoken English Travel: Approximately 20% Driver s licence: Required Portfolio: Strong portfolio desirable Visa sponsorship: No employment visa sponsorship or assistance offered, apart from local labour employment requirements Salary: Not specified in the vacancy Deadline: No fixed closing date published Recruitment model: Rolling interviews; job may close once a strong applicant pool has been established Application: Apply through the official TNC Workday vacancy. Conclusion The Strategic Content and Storytelling Manager – Africa Region position at The Nature Conservancy offers an experienced communications professional the opportunity to shape how one of the world s major conservation organizations tells its Africa story. This is not a routine communications officer role. The successful candidate will influence the editorial strategy of TNC Africa, establish storytelling priorities, produce high-level written and multimedia content, conduct field reporting, work with communities and scientists, engage donor audiences, coordinate external creative partners and use audience data to improve content performance. The role is particularly suited to professionals who combine journalism-quality storytelling with organizational communications strategy . Candidates with experience in journalism, documentary storytelling, editorial publishing, conservation, sustainability, development or nonprofit communications may find the position especially relevant. The minimum profile includes a bachelor s degree in a relevant field and at least seven years of related experience , or an equivalent combination of education and experience. TNC s preferred profile includes eight or more years of professional experience , a strong storytelling portfolio, field-reporting experience, multimedia capability, strong project management and knowledge of ethical and inclusive storytelling practices. The position can be based in Kenya, Tanzania, Gabon, Zambia, South Africa or Angola , but applicants should carefully note that TNC is not offering employment visa sponsorship or assistance for this role .
