title: GIST Graduate Scholarship 2027 in South Korea: Apply for Master’s, PhD and Integrated MS–PhD Programs with Full Tuition and Monthly Support
summary: Applications are now open for the Gwangju Institute of Science and Technology (GIST) Spring 2027 Graduate Admissions , giving international students the opportunity to pursue advanced study in South Korea through Master of Science, Doctor of Philosophy and Integrated Master’s–PhD programmes. GIST is accepting international applications from 7 September 2026 at 10:00 KST until 7 October 2026 at 17:00 KST . Applicants must complete the online application and submit all required materials before the deadline; GIST explicitly states that late applications are not accepted. The Spring semester begins in March 2027. One of the strongest features of GIST graduate admission is the financial-support system available to international graduate students. According to GIST’s official scholarship information, international students receive full tuition support together with monthly allowances, research-assistantship opportunities, health-insurance support and reimbursement for a one-way flight to Korea . However, applicants should understand that this does not necessarily mean every expense is covered: newly admitted students are normally charged a KRW 680,000 matriculation fee , although a waiver may be available for students with financial difficulties, and housing and utility costs can still apply. Application deadline: 7 October 2026 at 17:00 KST. Official GIST International Graduate Admissions website: GIST International Graduate Admissions Online application: Apply for Spring 2027 Graduate Admission About GIST Spring 2027 Graduate Admissions The Gwangju Institute of Science and Technology , widely known as GIST, is a science- and technology-focused graduate institution in Gwangju, South Korea. For Spring 2027, the university is recruiting international students across a broad range of science, engineering, technology and interdisciplinary academic fields. The admission window officially opened on: 7 September 2026 at 10:00 KST and will close on: 7 October 2026 at 17:00 KST. GIST’s official schedule indicates that applicants will subsequently go through document examination and academic review, with final admission results scheduled for 4 December 2026 . Successful applicants must complete enrollment by 4 January 2027 . GIST notes that these dates may be changed without prior notice. For Spring admission, applicants who have not yet completed their current degree must obtain their final qualification by approximately the first week of January 2027 , before enrollment at GIST. Degree Programs Available at GIST International applicants can apply for three main graduate pathways: Master of Science Program (M.S.) Doctor of Philosophy Program (Ph.D.) Integrated Master of Science and Doctor of Philosophy Program (M.S./Ph.D.) GIST states that students are expected to maintain full-time status and continuous registration until they complete their degree requirements. A Master’s programme normally takes approximately two years, while a PhD normally takes about four years. The maximum completion periods are three years for an M.S., seven years for a PhD and eight years for an integrated M.S./Ph.D. programme. Academic Fields and Graduate Departments GIST offers graduate study across a substantial range of scientific and technological disciplines. Current graduate academic areas listed by GIST include: Electrical Engineering and Computer Science Materials Science and Engineering Mechanical and Robotics Engineering Environment and Energy Engineering Life Sciences Physics and Photon Science Chemistry Biomedical Science and Engineering Artificial Intelligence Semiconductor Engineering AI Policy and Strategy Integrative Neuroscience and Physiology Mathematical Sciences The Mathematical Sciences programme is currently listed as M.S.-only . Applicants should review their intended department carefully before applying because departmental research interests, faculty availability and specific programme expectations may differ. GIST Scholarship and Financial Support for International Students A major attraction of graduate study at GIST is that international graduate students are provided with financial support through the university’s scholarship system. GIST’s official FAQ states that all international graduate students are granted the GIST scholarship without a separate scholarship application . This means that international applicants do not normally need to submit a completely separate funding application after applying for graduate admission. However, individual components of the support package have their own conditions, and not every possible expense associated with studying in Korea is automatically paid. Full Tuition Support GIST provides full tuition support to graduate students. The university’s scholarship page currently lists tuition of: KRW 3,607,000 per semester as fully supported. Applicants should rely on GIST’s current official financial-support page when preparing budgets because financial figures can be updated over time. One-Time Matriculation Fee Although tuition is supported, newly admitted students are normally required to pay a separate: KRW 680,000 matriculation fee. The fee is paid at enrollment and is non-refundable. This distinction is important when describing the opportunity as “fully funded.” GIST may waive the matriculation fee for students who demonstrate financial difficulties. Applicants who want to request a waiver must: Indicate the request in the online application; and Upload the required recommendation letter from the department chair of their current or most recently attended university. The GIST Admissions Committee considers the waiver request alongside the admission application. Applicants should therefore not assume that the KRW 680,000 fee is automatically waived. Monthly Student Allowance International graduate students may receive a monthly student allowance. GIST currently lists: Master’s students: KRW 140,000 per month PhD students: KRW 295,000 per month The university notes that students must generally have completed at least nine credits in the previous semester for the student allowance and meal allowance. New students should therefore carefully check how first-semester payments are administered rather than assuming every conditional allowance begins immediately under exactly the same rules. Monthly Meal Allowance GIST currently lists a meal allowance of approximately: KRW 100,000 per month. As with the student allowance, the university states that the previous-semester nine-credit requirement applies. International Student Allowance International students may additionally receive: KRW 120,000 per month as an international-student allowance. GIST states that eligibility for this payment requires a previous-semester GPA of at least: 3.0 out of 4.5. This is another reason applicants should distinguish between guaranteed admission funding and allowances that may depend on maintaining specified academic conditions. Research Assistantship Opportunities Students participating in research projects may also receive research-assistantship funding. GIST’s current financial-support page lists historical average research-assistantship figures, as of 2022, of approximately: KRW 6.4 million per year for M.S. students KRW 13.74 million per year for PhD students These figures are described as averages rather than guaranteed fixed awards for every student. The actual research-assistantship amount can therefore depend on factors such as: Research project participation Laboratory Department Supervisor Available research funding Student circumstances Applicants should not add the historical average automatically to their expected annual income without confirming the current arrangement with their prospective department. Health-Insurance Support GIST provides health-insurance support to international students. The university currently states that it supports: 60% of the Korean National Health Insurance fee for international students. An annual medical checkup is also listed among the support provisions. Because GIST pays only part of the insurance cost, applicants should budget for the remaining portion. One-Way Flight Reimbursement to South Korea Incoming international students are eligible for reimbursement for: A one-way flight to Korea. GIST notes that this is available for the first use only. Applicants should keep all required travel documentation and follow the university’s reimbursement procedures rather than assuming the ticket will necessarily be purchased directly by GIST. Housing at GIST GIST provides access to student housing, but housing should not be confused with a completely free accommodation scholarship. The official scholarship page lists graduate dormitories and accommodation for married students with applicable: Monthly charges Deposits Utility costs GIST also warns that waiting periods may occur and that housing fees may increase over time. Therefore, international applicants should budget for accommodation even though campus housing can make living expenses considerably more manageable. Is the GIST Scholarship Really Fully Funded? The programme provides a very comprehensive graduate funding package , including full tuition support and several forms of living and research support. However, the phrase “fully funded” should be used with appropriate qualification. GIST confirms that international graduate students receive: Full tuition support Monthly student allowance Meal allowance International-student allowance Research-assistantship opportunities Health-insurance support One-way flight reimbursement At the same time: A KRW 680,000 matriculation fee normally applies unless waived. Housing is not automatically free. Utility costs can apply. Research-assistantship amounts are not identical for every student. Some monthly allowances require satisfactory credits or GPA. Health-insurance support covers 60%, not necessarily 100%. The most accurate description is therefore that GIST provides substantial or comprehensive graduate scholarship support with full tuition , rather than claiming that every possible personal expense will automatically be covered. Who Can Apply for Spring 2027? The Spring 2027 announcement states that applicants should hold, or expect to hold, the appropriate final degree before enrolling at GIST. For Spring 2027, final degree completion should occur by approximately the first week of January 2027 . In practical terms: Applicants to Master’s-level study should have the appropriate undergraduate qualification. Doctoral applicants should have the appropriate prior graduate qualification required by their programme. Applicants who are still completing their degree can apply using evidence of expected graduation. GIST’s required-document guidance specifically allows applicants who have not yet graduated to replace the final diploma temporarily with an official expected-graduation certificate or university letter showing the applicant’s name, intended degree and expected conferral date. Important Nationality Rule GIST’s Spring 2027 announcement identifies the call as an international admission track and specifically states: Korean citizens holding dual citizenship are not eligible. International applicants from countries around the world can otherwise apply subject to the programme requirements. Applicants with unusual nationality, residency or dual-citizenship circumstances should check directly with GIST rather than assuming eligibility. English-Language Requirements English is used as a language of instruction at GIST, and international applicants are normally expected to demonstrate English proficiency. The current minimum accepted scores are: Test Minimum score TOEFL iBT 80 TOEFL PBT 550 Academic IELTS 6.5 TOEIC 750 NEW TEPS 285 English-language test results must normally have been taken within two years before the application deadline . Who Can Receive an English-Test Exemption? GIST lists exemptions for: Native-born citizens of Australia, Canada, Ireland, New Zealand, the United Kingdom or the United States; and Applicants who hold a bachelor’s or higher degree from a university physically located in one of those countries, subject to prior GIST approval. Applicants should not assume that simply completing a degree taught in English in another country automatically provides a permanent exemption. Conditional Admission Without an Official English Test GIST does provide a limited conditional-admission mechanism. Applicants who cannot take an official English test because, for example, testing is unavailable in their country or unavoidable circumstances make testing impossible may submit a: Certificate of English Language Proficiency issued by the president or dean of their previous institution. The document must confirm that the medium of instruction was English. However, students admitted conditionally must subsequently submit an official English score meeting GIST’s standard within six months after admission . Failure to do so can result in removal from the university register. GIST also strongly recommends obtaining an official English test because Korean immigration authorities or Korean diplomatic missions may require evidence of language proficiency during the visa process. Required Application Documents Applicants should prepare all mandatory materials before the 7 October deadline. GIST currently requires: Completed online application Official degree certificates Official academic transcripts Two recommendation letters Official English-proficiency evidence or qualifying alternative Copy of the applicant’s passport Applicants should also pay close attention to document certification requirements. Academic Certificates and Transcripts Applicants must provide academic certificates and transcripts covering their relevant undergraduate and graduate studies. GIST encourages applicants to prepare documents with: Apostille authentication, or Korean embassy/consular authentication because successful applicants will eventually need authenticated academic records. Transcripts should show: Courses completed Grades or marks Cumulative GPA Grading system Class rank where available If the institution’s grading scale is not printed on the transcript, applicants should provide an additional document explaining the grading system. Applicants to doctoral programmes should be prepared to provide documentation for both their bachelor’s and master’s qualifications. Special Requirement for Applicants Educated in China Applicants who graduated from universities in China can use the appropriate verification report issued through CSSD/CHSI (学信网) for degree and transcript verification in accordance with GIST’s admissions guidance. Two Recommendation Letters Two recommendations are required. GIST currently accepts recommendation letters electronically through Google Forms . During the online application, applicants register their referees. After the application fee has been paid, applicants can trigger an automated email containing the recommendation submission link. Referees must complete GIST’s designated recommendation form and submit their letters by the application deadline. Eligible referees include people who have worked closely with the applicant in an academic or professional capacity, such as: Professors Faculty members Research supervisors Professional supervisors Applicants should contact referees early because an otherwise complete application can be affected if recommendation letters arrive late. Application Fee An application fee is mandatory . GIST’s FAQ explicitly states that applications are not processed as valid until the required application fee has been paid. The currently retrieved admissions pages do not state the amount in the information reviewed here, so applicants should confirm the amount directly within the 2027 online application system. How to Apply for GIST Spring 2027 The application process is completed online. Step 1: Choose Your Program Review the GIST graduate departments and determine whether you are applying for: M.S. Ph.D. Integrated M.S./Ph.D. Applicants should also investigate the research interests of their chosen department. Step 2: Complete the Online Application Applications are submitted through GIST’s designated online system. Open the GIST Spring 2027 application portal GIST recommends using a Windows-based computer because its application system is optimized for Windows. Step 3: Pay the Application Fee The application fee must be paid before certain parts of the application process, including electronic recommendation requests, can proceed. Step 4: Upload Required Documents All application documents must be in: English, or Korean. Documents issued in another language must be translated into English or Korean by the issuing institution or a public notary. Step 5: Make Sure Referees Submit Recommendations Both recommendation letters must arrive by the deadline. Step 6: Monitor Your Email The GIST Admissions Team or relevant department may contact applicants for additional information or an interview where necessary. Step 7: Receive the Admission Decision Spring 2027 admission results are scheduled for: 4 December 2026. Step 8: Complete Enrollment Successful candidates must accept their offer, submit enrollment documents and pay the applicable matriculation fee by the enrollment deadline. For Spring 2027, the enrollment deadline is scheduled for: 4 January 2027. Step 9: Submit Verified Academic Documents Successful applicants must eventually submit properly authenticated academic certificates, generally through apostille or Korean consular authentication. Step 10: Apply for a Korean Student Visa After admission and enrollment documentation is issued, international students can proceed with their Korean student-visa application using the Certificate of Admission provided by GIST. Spring 2027 Admission Timeline Stage Date Applications open 7 September 2026, 10:00 KST Application deadline 7 October 2026, 17:00 KST Document examination Approximately 15 days Documents review Approximately 30 days Admission results 4 December 2026 Enrollment deadline 4 January 2027 Spring semester Begins March 2027 The university notes that the schedule may change without prior notice. Important Points Applicants Should Not Overlook The GIST scholarship is highly attractive, but prospective students should understand several details before applying. First, full tuition does not mean every expense is free . The KRW 680,000 matriculation fee normally applies unless the university approves a waiver. Housing and utilities also involve costs. Second, some monthly allowances depend on maintaining academic requirements such as credit completion or GPA. Third, research-assistantship figures published by GIST are averages, not a guaranteed identical amount for every graduate student. Fourth, applicants need two recommendation letters , and the letters must arrive electronically by the application deadline. Finally, an official English-language test should be taken early whenever possible because GIST will not accept late application documents after the deadline. Key Information at a Glance University: Gwangju Institute of Science and Technology (GIST) Study country: South Korea Location: Gwangju Entry: Spring 2027 Application opening: 7 September 2026, 10:00 KST Deadline: 7 October 2026, 17:00 KST Degrees: M.S., Ph.D. and Integrated M.S./Ph.D. Study status: Full-time International students: Eligible Tuition: Fully supported Matriculation fee: KRW 680,000 unless an approved waiver applies Monthly student allowance: KRW 140,000 for M.S.; KRW 295,000 for Ph.D. Meal allowance: Approximately KRW 100,000 per month International-student allowance: KRW 120,000 per month subject to academic conditions Research assistantship: Available to students participating in research projects; amount varies Health insurance: 60% of Korean National Health Insurance fee supported Flight: One-way flight reimbursement for incoming international students English minimum: TOEFL iBT 80, TOEFL PBT 550, IELTS Academic 6.5, TOEIC 750 or NEW TEPS 285 Recommendation letters: Two Results: Scheduled for 4 December 2026 Enrollment deadline: 4 January 2027 Conclusion The GIST Spring 2027 Graduate Admissions and Scholarship opportunity offers international students a strong route to advanced science and technology study in South Korea. Students can apply for Master’s, PhD or Integrated Master’s–PhD programmes in fields ranging from electrical engineering, computer science and artificial intelligence to life sciences, biomedical engineering, environment and energy, physics, chemistry, semiconductor engineering, neuroscience and other interdisciplinary areas. The funding package is substantial. International graduate students receive full tuition support without having to submit a separate scholarship application, together with monthly allowances, potential research-assistantship funding, partial health-insurance support and a one-way flight reimbursement. Applicants should nevertheless budget carefully. The normal KRW 680,000 matriculation fee , housing costs, utility expenses and the conditional nature of some allowances mean that “fully funded” should not be interpreted as meaning that every personal expense is automatically paid. International applicants interested in Spring 2027 should begin preparing immediately, particularly their academic records, English-language results and two recommendations. GIST requires all application materials to be received by the deadline, and late submissions are not accepted. Final application deadline: 7 October 2026 at 17:00 KST. title: Sustainable Research Pathways 2026–2027: U.S. Research Collaboration and Paid Summer Experience Opportunities for Students, Faculty and Project Leaders
summary: The Sustainable Research Pathways (SRP) 2026–2027 program is inviting applications from eligible students, faculty members, principal investigators, and project leaders across the United States and its territories for a research collaboration and professional development opportunity designed to connect emerging researchers with established scientific projects. The program provides a structured environment for participants to build research collaborations, explore career opportunities, develop professional networks, and potentially participate in a 10-week paid summer research experience in 2027 . Through workshops, mentoring, cohort activities, and research engagement, SRP aims to help students and faculty connect with projects led by researchers working with U.S. Department of Energy (DOE) National Laboratories and the National Science Foundation (NSF) National AI Research Resource (NAIRR) pilot, among other participating projects. Applications for the 2026–2027 cycle are currently open, with applications for principal investigators/project leaders, faculty, and students due September 30, 2026 . What Is the Sustainable Research Pathways Program? Sustainable Research Pathways is a comprehensive research collaboration program created to connect U.S.-based researchers and project leaders with students and faculty from academic institutions throughout the United States and its territories. The program is designed around the idea that meaningful research collaborations can help students launch scientific and technical careers while also giving researchers and faculty access to new talent, perspectives, and collaborative possibilities. Rather than functioning solely as a traditional internship or academic placement, SRP provides opportunities for participants to meet potential collaborators, explore research projects, participate in professional community-building activities, and potentially continue their engagement through a summer research experience. The 2026–2027 program brings together several tracks, allowing participation from different groups within the research ecosystem. History and Development of Sustainable Research Pathways Sustainable Research Pathways was initially established in 2015 through a partnership with Lawrence Berkeley National Laboratory (LBNL) . Since its creation, the program has expanded considerably. In 2022 , SRP developed into a multi-laboratory program through the U.S. Department of Energy s Exascale Computing Project (ECP) . In 2023 , the program expanded beyond ECP projects to include additional computational and data science projects. These activities were coordinated through the Computational Research Leadership Council (CRLC) . The program has continued to receive support from the U.S. Department of Energy s Office of Advanced Scientific Computing Research through the Partnering for Scientific-Software Ecosystem Opportunities (PESO) project and the Consortium for the Advancement of Scientific Software (CASS) . In 2025 , SRP expanded further by incorporating projects associated with the National Science Foundation s National AI Research Resource (NAIRR) pilot and the High Performance Software Foundation (HPSF) . The 2026–2027 cycle therefore represents a broader research collaboration environment involving students, faculty, project leaders, and projects connected with major U.S. scientific and computational research initiatives. SRP 2026–2027 Project, PI and Mentor Track The Project/PI/Mentor Track is intended for principal investigators and project leaders who have active projects funded through eligible NAIRR Pilot or U.S. Department of Energy National Laboratories Computing Sciences programs. Researchers and project leaders participating in this track can potentially be matched with students and faculty interested in contributing to research projects. For participating project leaders, the program provides an opportunity to: Connect with exceptional students and faculty. Explore potential research collaborations. Introduce students to active scientific and computational projects. Build longer-term academic and professional relationships. Participate in the SRP Matching and Exploratory Workshop. Identify potential collaborators for summer research activities. If a successful match is established, project leaders may have the opportunity to work collaboratively with selected faculty members and students. Faculty Track The Faculty Track is designed for full-time faculty members who are interested in leading student teams and potentially collaborating with projects connected to NAIRR and DOE National Laboratories. Faculty members working with students from different academic institutions are particularly encouraged to participate. This track can provide faculty with a structured mechanism for connecting their students to broader research projects and professional communities. Faculty participants may have the opportunity to: Lead student teams. Connect students with research project leaders. Explore collaborations with NAIRR-related projects. Explore collaborations with DOE National Laboratories projects. Participate in the November 2026 Matching Workshop. Build relationships with researchers and other faculty members. Support students as they explore research and career pathways. The cross-institutional nature of the program also provides an opportunity for faculty and students from different academic environments to engage with one another. Student Track The Student Track is intended for eligible students who are studying at accredited U.S. academic institutions and who are not applying as part of an SRP faculty team. The program specifically identifies the following student groups as eligible to apply: Community college students. Undergraduate students. Graduate students. Students can apply independently rather than having to participate through an SRP faculty team. For students interested in research, computational science, data science, artificial intelligence, scientific software, or related areas, the program provides an opportunity to explore potential research collaborations and develop professional relationships with researchers and faculty. Potential 10-Week Summer Research Experience One of the significant opportunities associated with SRP is the potential for matched faculty and students to participate in a 10-week onsite summer experience in 2027 . Participants who are successfully matched with project leaders may have the opportunity to spend the summer working on research activities connected to their selected project. The experience is described as potentially paid, meaning eligible participants may have access to a paid summer research opportunity depending on the specific match and arrangements. The summer experience is expected to provide participants with exposure to real research environments while allowing them to work with project leaders and other members of the research community. Matching and Exploratory Workshop A central component of SRP is the Matching and Exploratory Workshop , scheduled for November 3–6, 2026 . The workshop is designed to give project leaders, faculty, and students an opportunity to meet, communicate, discuss research interests, and explore possible collaborations. Rather than participants being matched without interaction, the workshop creates a dedicated environment where individuals can learn more about available research projects and potential collaborators. The workshop can therefore play an important role in helping participants determine whether their research interests and skills align with particular projects. SRP Program Benefits The Sustainable Research Pathways program offers several activities and potential benefits throughout the 2026–2027 cycle. 1. Pre-Workshop Q A Webinar Participants will have access to a Q A webinar before the main matching workshop. This provides an opportunity for prospective participants to better understand the program and ask questions about participation. 2. Matching and Exploratory Workshop The interactive workshop gives participants an opportunity to meet researchers, faculty members, project leaders, and students and discuss potential collaborations. 3. Potential Paid Summer Experience Students and faculty who are successfully matched with project leaders may have the opportunity to participate in a 10-week onsite summer experience in 2027 . The summer experience may be paid, providing participants with both research exposure and potential financial support for their summer participation. 4. Professional Community Onboarding SRP includes onboarding into a professional community, helping participants become familiar with the broader network associated with the program. This can help participants establish relationships beyond their immediate academic institution. 5. Summer Kick-Off Event The program includes a summer kick-off event intended to bring members of the cohort together as summer research activities begin. 6. Midterm Practice and Check-In Participants will take part in a midterm practice and check-in during the summer. This provides an opportunity for members of the cohort to reflect on their experiences and remain connected throughout the research period. 7. End-of-Summer Celebration The program also includes an end-of-summer celebration marking the conclusion of the summer research experience. 8. CULTIVATE Conversations After the summer program, participants can continue engaging with the SRP community through CULTIVATE Conversations , which are described as virtual seminars and meet-ups. This post-summer engagement can help maintain relationships established during the program. 9. Potential Conference Presentation Funding Some funding will be available to support participants in presenting their summer research results at a scientific conference. This provides an additional opportunity for participants to share their research outcomes with the wider scientific community and gain experience communicating research findings in a professional setting. SRP 2026–2027 Important Dates Applicants should carefully observe the program s schedule because different activities take place from September 2026 through spring 2028. Applications Applications are currently open. Application deadline for PIs, faculty and students: September 30, 2026 Applicants should ensure that their applications are completed and submitted before the deadline. Participant Q A Webinar Date: September 24, 2026 Time: 10:00 AM PT A Participant Q A Webinar will be held to provide information and answer questions about the program. DOE Mentor Q A Webinar Date: September 24, 2026 Time: 1:30 PM PT A separate Q A webinar will be available for DOE mentors. Welcome Reception Date: November 3, 2026 The welcome reception will take place at the beginning of the program s main November activities. Matching Workshop Dates: November 3–6, 2026 The Matching Workshop will provide participants with an opportunity to meet and explore potential research collaborations. Onboarding Period: Winter/Spring 2027 Participants will complete onboarding activities ahead of the summer research period. Research Activities Period: Summer 2027 Matched participants may participate in the program s summer research activities, including the potential 10-week onsite experience. Conference Presentations Period: Spring 2028 Participants may have an opportunity to present results from their summer research at scientific conferences, with some funds available for conference presentation support. Who Can Apply for Sustainable Research Pathways 2026–2027? The program has separate participation tracks, and eligibility depends on the applicant s role. Principal Investigators and Project Leaders The Project/PI/Mentor Track is intended for principal investigators and project leaders with active NAIRR Pilot or U.S. Department of Energy National Laboratories Computing Sciences funded projects . Faculty Members The Faculty Track is open to full-time faculty who can lead student teams and potentially collaborate with NAIRR and DOE National Laboratories projects. Faculty working with students from a variety of institutions are encouraged to apply. Students The Student Track is open to: Community college students. Undergraduate students. Graduate students. Students must be studying at an accredited U.S. academic institution and must not be applying as part of an SRP faculty team. Country and Geographic Eligibility Sustainable Research Pathways is specifically designed for the United States and its territories . The program description states that it connects U.S. researchers and project leaders with students and faculty from across the United States and its territories. Student applicants must attend an accredited U.S. academic institution. Therefore, this is not presented as a general worldwide opportunity . Prospective applicants should carefully review their institutional and program eligibility before applying. The available information does not specify eligibility based on race or ethnicity. How the SRP Program Can Support Career Development A major objective of Sustainable Research Pathways is to help participants build pathways toward research and scientific careers. For students, participating in research activities can provide exposure to professional research environments, while interaction with project leaders and faculty can help them better understand potential career directions. For faculty, the program can facilitate collaboration between institutions and research teams. For project leaders, SRP can provide a structured environment for engaging with students and faculty who may contribute new perspectives and skills to their research projects. The combination of research activities, professional community-building, workshops, mentoring, and potential conference participation makes the program broader than a single summer placement. How the Matching Process Can Create Collaboration Opportunities The matching component is particularly important because SRP is structured around connecting participants with potential research collaborators. During the November 2026 workshop, participants can meet and discuss potential research interests and collaborations. This interaction allows students and faculty to learn more about research projects while allowing project leaders and mentors to identify potential participants whose interests and backgrounds align with their work. Successful matches may subsequently lead to the 10-week summer research experience planned for 2027. Application Process Applications for the three main tracks are submitted through the SRP application system. Applicants should select the appropriate track based on their role: Project/PI/Mentor Track for eligible principal investigators and project leaders. Faculty Track for eligible full-time faculty. Student Track for eligible community college, undergraduate, and graduate students. Applicants should provide accurate information and ensure that they meet the relevant requirements before submitting their applications. Application deadline: September 30, 2026 Q A Webinar Registration The September 24 Q A sessions can provide prospective participants with additional information about the program. The Participant Q A Webinar is scheduled for 10:00 AM PT, while the DOE Mentor Q A Webinar is scheduled for 1:30 PM PT. Prospective applicants who have questions about participation, tracks, matching, or program activities can use the relevant registration pages provided by the organizers. APPLY HERE Why Applicants Should Review Their Eligibility Carefully Because Sustainable Research Pathways contains multiple tracks, applicants should not assume that the same eligibility requirements apply to everyone. A student applicant, for example, must meet the requirements for the Student Track, including enrollment at an accredited U.S. academic institution. Similarly, faculty applicants must meet the requirements specified for the Faculty Track, while project leaders and principal investigators must have qualifying active projects for the Project/PI/Mentor Track. Reviewing the appropriate track before applying can help applicants submit their applications through the correct pathway. Visit HERE to learn more about the Sustainable Research Pathways 2026–2027. Sustainable Research Pathways 2026–2027 Timeline at a Glance Activity Date/Period Applications Open Now Application Deadline September 30, 2026 Participant Q A Webinar September 24, 2026, 10:00 AM PT DOE Mentor Q A Webinar September 24, 2026, 1:30 PM PT Welcome Reception November 3, 2026 Matching Workshop November 3–6, 2026 Onboarding Winter/Spring 2027 Research Activities Summer 2027 Conference Presentations Spring 2028 How to Apply for Sustainable Research Pathways 2026–2027 Eligible applicants can submit their applications through the official SRP application portal. Applicants should make sure they select the correct track and complete the application before the September 30, 2026 deadline. Conclusion The Sustainable Research Pathways 2026–2027 program provides a structured platform for connecting students, faculty members, principal investigators, and research project leaders across the United States and its territories. Through its Project/PI/Mentor, Faculty, and Student Tracks, the program creates opportunities for participants to explore research collaborations, develop professional relationships, participate in an interactive matching workshop, and potentially take part in a 10-week paid onsite summer research experience in 2027 . The program also extends beyond the summer through professional community onboarding, cohort-wide activities, CULTIVATE Conversations, and potential financial support for presenting summer research results at scientific conferences. With applications due on September 30, 2026 , eligible students, faculty members, and qualifying research project leaders should review the requirements for their respective tracks and submit their applications through the official application portal before the deadline. The program is intended for applicants connected to the United States and its territories. The provided information does not specify race or ethnicity restrictions. title: University of Salford Postgraduate Research Degrees: PhD and Doctoral Study Opportunities in the UK
summary: The University of Salford in the United Kingdom offers a broad range of postgraduate research opportunities for students seeking to undertake advanced academic research and develop specialist expertise in their chosen field. Its postgraduate research community spans disciplines including arts and creative technologies, business, management and law, health and society, science, engineering and the environment. Through its research centres, academic schools and Doctoral School, the University provides postgraduate researchers with opportunities to undertake original research, work with experienced supervisors, develop specialist skills and build academic and professional networks. For prospective researchers looking to pursue a PhD, professional doctorate, MPhil, MSc by Research or another postgraduate research qualification in the UK , Salford provides multiple research pathways across a wide range of subject areas. About University of Salford Postgraduate Research The University of Salford describes its research environment as being focused on addressing complex challenges facing society through pioneering research and solutions-focused enterprise. Postgraduate researchers become part of a large research community distributed across the University s research centres and academic schools. Researchers also have access to the University s Doctoral School , which provides support and training intended to help students develop as researchers. The University s postgraduate research environment is designed not only around academic study but also around the development of research skills, professional networks and specialist expertise that can be applied beyond academia. For international students, the opportunity also provides exposure to the UK s higher education and research environment while allowing them to work alongside researchers from different academic and professional backgrounds. What Is a Research Degree? A research degree is an advanced academic qualification centred on independent investigation rather than primarily classroom-based study. At the University of Salford, postgraduate research students are expected to investigate an innovative or novel research area and make an original contribution to their chosen field. Under the guidance of academic supervisors, researchers take significant responsibility for developing and conducting their research. This structure gives students considerable freedom to shape their research questions, methodology and contribution within the requirements of their chosen programme. Research degrees can be particularly relevant to graduates who want to: Develop specialist expertise in a particular academic field. Conduct original research into an emerging or under-researched issue. Prepare for an academic or research-oriented career. Develop advanced analytical and problem-solving skills. Explore an interdisciplinary research topic. Build an international academic and professional network. Develop expertise that can also be applied in industry, government, policy, technology, creative industries or other professional environments. The University offers different types of postgraduate research qualifications depending on the applicant s academic objectives and selected research pathway. Postgraduate Research Degrees Available at Salford The University of Salford offers both master s-level research degrees and doctoral degrees. Master s-Level Research Degrees Master s-level research programmes include: Master of Science by Research (MSc by Research) Master of Philosophy (MPhil) These programmes allow students to undertake substantial independent research under academic supervision. A research master s degree can be suitable for graduates who want to develop advanced research capabilities or explore a specific topic in considerable depth. It can also provide preparation for further doctoral-level study. Doctoral Degrees The University also offers several doctoral-level qualifications, including: PhD Doctor of Professional Practice (DProf) Doctor of Business Administration (DBA) Doctoral degrees represent the highest academic qualifications awarded by universities in the UK. A PhD, for example, normally requires the researcher to investigate a specific research question or problem and make an original contribution to knowledge in the field. The exact duration, structure and requirements of a research degree depend on the specific programme and pathway selected. Prospective applicants should therefore review the requirements of their chosen course carefully before applying. Research Opportunities Across Multiple Academic Fields One of the major features of postgraduate research at Salford is the breadth of research specialisms available. The University s research activity is organised across four broad academic areas: Arts, Media and Creative Technology Business, Management and Law Health and Society Science, Engineering and Environment This range allows prospective postgraduate researchers to investigate subjects extending from creative technologies and communication to artificial intelligence, business transformation, health, robotics, environmental sustainability and biomedical research. Arts, Media and Creative Technology Research The University s School of Arts, Media and Creative Technology provides a research environment for students interested in creative practice, technology, media, culture, design and related interdisciplinary subjects. The School attracts researchers from different parts of the world and promotes collaboration, interdisciplinary research and international networking. Its research environment also connects academic research with real-world challenges and creative practice. The University highlights its facilities and spaces, including the New Adelphi building and the Salford International Innovation Studio at MediaCity , as part of the environment available to researchers, artists, designers and other creative practitioners. Creative Technologies Research Centre The Creative Technologies Research Centre explores the intersection between creative practices and emerging technologies. Research can involve areas such as: Film Music Performance Broadcasting Games Immersive media Artificial intelligence Machine learning Other emerging creative technologies This area may be particularly relevant to researchers interested in how technology is transforming creative production, cultural experiences and media industries. English Research Centre and Practice as Research Research within English and Practice as Research takes an interdisciplinary approach to literature, culture and creative practice. The research environment explores hybrid, experimental and emerging forms of work while connecting academic research with cultural life beyond the University. Research interests include topics such as: Conflict writing in Northern Ireland Victorian sensation fiction Early Modern Drama Representations of serial killers in film and fiction African modernism Place names and their hidden meanings Neglected and transgressive authors Experimental cultural practices This provides opportunities for researchers interested in literature, cultural studies, creative practice and interdisciplinary humanities research. Politics and Contemporary History Research Centre The Politics and Contemporary History Research Centre brings together research interests covering political and historical themes, particularly within the broad area of international security. Areas of interest include: International politics European party politics Political ideologies Intelligence studies Military history Counter-insurgency Counter-terrorism International security Political and historical developments in Europe Political developments in the Middle East Political developments in Latin America Political developments in Asia This research environment may appeal to prospective researchers interested in contemporary political and historical issues. Art and Design Research and Engagement The University s Art and Design research activities include theoretical and practice-based creative investigations. Research areas include topics such as: Design for health and wellbeing Games for social change Design against crime Creative practice Art and design research The area brings together established researchers and early-career researchers working across different aspects of art and design. For enquiries concerning postgraduate research in Arts, Media and Creative Technology, the University provides the email address pgr-supportsam@salford.ac.uk . Business, Management and Law Research The University of Salford s business, management and law research environment is designed for postgraduate researchers interested in organisations, business transformation, entrepreneurship, finance, sustainability, technology and related areas. Salford Business School encourages postgraduate researchers to think critically, challenge existing assumptions and investigate issues relevant to both academic research and professional practice. Research themes broadly align with the University s innovation strategy and include: Business change Entrepreneurial thinking Financial technology and FinTech Ethical working Sustainable working Digital transformation Business innovation Organisational development Centre for Sustainable Innovation The Centre for Sustainable Innovation supports research and collaboration around sustainability and innovation. The Centre provides businesses with access to research, specialist expertise and opportunities for collaboration and learning. For postgraduate researchers, this broader research environment can provide opportunities to investigate the relationship between business, innovation, technology and sustainability. Applicants interested in postgraduate research in Business, Management and Law can contact pgr-supportsbs@salford.ac.uk for further information. Health and Society Research The University of Salford also offers postgraduate research opportunities in health and society. Research within this area is organised into three major research centres: Centre for Human Movement and Rehabilitation This research centre focuses on human movement, rehabilitation and related areas of health research. Researchers in this area can investigate issues connected with movement, rehabilitation, physical function and related health and wellbeing challenges. Centre for Applied Health Research The Centre for Applied Health Research provides a research environment focused on applying research knowledge to health-related challenges. This can provide opportunities for researchers interested in evidence-based approaches to improving health and healthcare. Centre for Research on Inclusive Society This research centre focuses on issues connected with inclusion and society. Its research environment provides opportunities for postgraduate researchers interested in social inclusion and related challenges affecting individuals and communities. Prospective postgraduate researchers interested in Health and Society can contact pgr-supportshas@salford.ac.uk for further information. Science, Engineering and Environment Research The School of Science, Engineering and Environment (SEE) provides another major area of postgraduate research at Salford. Researchers in this School work across a wide range of scientific and engineering disciplines, including computing, artificial intelligence, robotics, environmental research, biomedical science, energy and sustainable built environments. The University s interdisciplinary research centres include the following areas. Acoustics Research The Acoustics Research Centre and Laboratories conducts research into acoustics and its applications. Research focuses on areas connected with: Health Wellbeing Accessibility Industry Sound Acoustic environments The work aims to support improvements in how sound is experienced and managed in different environments. Autonomous Systems and Advanced Robotics The Autonomous Systems Advanced Robotics (ASAR) research area focuses on developments in autonomous systems and robotics. Research includes subjects such as: Autonomous vehicles Robotics Soft robotics Autonomous technologies Advanced robotic systems This area may be particularly relevant to applicants with academic backgrounds in engineering, robotics, computer science or related disciplines. Informatics Research Centre The Informatics Research Centre focuses on computing and engineering sciences. Research areas include: Computer science Data science Artificial intelligence Software engineering Cybersecurity Computing and engineering applications The Centre provides opportunities for researchers interested in technologies that underpin modern digital systems and services. Areas highlighted by the University include: Cancer diagnosis Cancer prevention Cardio-respiratory physiology Biomedical science Health-related research Researchers interested in biomedical and health sciences can explore the Centre s research activities when identifying potential research topics and supervisors. Energy House Laboratories The University s Energy House laboratories focus on sustainable built environments and the transition towards low-carbon and net-zero housing. Research areas include: Sustainable housing Low-carbon building design Net-zero housing Building materials Smart technology Energy consumption in homes Environmental impacts of buildings This research environment may be relevant to applicants interested in sustainability, construction, engineering, energy, architecture, building technology and environmental research. For enquiries about research opportunities within Science, Engineering and Environment, applicants can contact pgr-supportssee@salford.ac.uk . Finding a Potential PhD Supervisor at the University of Salford Finding an appropriate supervisor is an important part of planning postgraduate research. The University of Salford encourages prospective researchers to identify academics whose expertise closely matches their proposed research area. Applicants can use the University s staff directory to search for academics according to their research specialism and review individual academic profiles. When identifying a potential supervisor, applicants should consider: Research expertise: Look for academics whose research interests overlap with your proposed topic. Research methodology: Consider whether the academic has experience with the methods or approaches relevant to your proposed research. Research centre: Check whether the academic is connected to a research centre that supports your subject area. Academic publications: Reviewing an academic s research publications can help applicants understand their current research interests. Research proposal alignment: Your proposed research should have a clear connection with the expertise of the prospective supervisor. Interdisciplinary opportunities: Where appropriate, consider academics whose research crosses multiple disciplines. Selecting an appropriate supervisor can help applicants better understand whether their proposed project fits the University s existing research environment. Scholarships and Funding for Postgraduate Research The University of Salford provides scholarships and funding opportunities that can help students meet the costs associated with postgraduate research. However, an important point for prospective applicants is that scholarship applications are invited after applicants have been accepted onto a research degree course , according to the University s postgraduate research information. This means applicants interested in funding should not necessarily treat the scholarship process as separate from the admission process. Prospective researchers should first identify an appropriate research degree, review its admission requirements and investigate the University s available funding opportunities. Funding availability, eligibility criteria and application deadlines can vary between scholarships and research opportunities. Applicants should therefore check the University s current fees and funding information for the specific scholarship they intend to pursue. Who Can Apply for University of Salford Postgraduate Research? The opportunity is relevant to prospective postgraduate researchers seeking master s-level research or doctoral study in the United Kingdom . The specific academic requirements depend on the individual research degree and course selected. Applicants should therefore review the entry requirements for their chosen programme rather than assuming that one set of qualifications applies to every research degree. The research opportunities can be relevant to applicants with academic backgrounds in areas such as: Arts and humanities Media and creative technology English and literature Politics and contemporary history Art and design Business Management Law Entrepreneurship Finance and FinTech Health Rehabilitation Social sciences Computer science Data science Artificial intelligence Software engineering Cybersecurity Engineering Robotics Environmental science Biomedical sciences Energy Sustainable construction and the built environment International applicants should also check the University s specific international admissions, English-language and immigration requirements where applicable. Nationality and Geographic Eligibility The information provided for this opportunity does not specify a restriction to a particular nationality, race or continent for postgraduate research applicants. The University presents its postgraduate research environment as an international community, with students drawn from different parts of the world. Therefore, applicants from Africa, Asia, Europe, North America, South America, Oceania and other regions may be able to apply, provided they meet the academic, programme-specific and other applicable admission requirements. Nationality eligibility can differ for individual scholarships or funding schemes, however. Applicants should therefore distinguish between admission to a postgraduate research programme and eligibility for a particular scholarship . How to Apply for Postgraduate Research at the University of Salford Prospective applicants should begin by identifying a research area that closely matches their academic background and long-term research interests. A typical preparation process can include the following steps: Step 1: Identify Your Research Area Consider the subject you want to investigate and determine which University of Salford school or research centre best matches your interests. The University s four broad research areas provide a useful starting point: Arts, Media and Creative Technology Business, Management and Law Health and Society Science, Engineering and Environment Step 2: Explore Relevant Research Centres Once you identify your field, examine the relevant research centres and their current areas of expertise. This can help you determine whether the University has appropriate academic expertise and research facilities for your proposed project. Step 3: Identify a Potential Supervisor Use the University s staff directory to search for academics working within your area of interest. Review their research profiles and consider how closely their expertise aligns with your proposed research. Step 4: Choose the Appropriate Research Degree Determine whether your academic and professional objectives are best suited to: MSc by Research MPhil PhD DProf DBA The appropriate qualification will depend on the research topic, academic background and intended career direction. Step 5: Review Course-Specific Requirements Before submitting an application, carefully check the entry requirements for your selected research programme. Requirements can differ according to the course and applicant circumstances. Step 6: Prepare Your Research Materials Prospective researchers should prepare the documents requested by their selected programme. Depending on the programme, this may include academic qualifications, transcripts, research information or proposal materials and evidence of English-language proficiency where applicable. Applicants should follow the University s current application instructions rather than relying on requirements for another research programme. Step 7: Apply for Admission After identifying the appropriate research degree and preparing the required materials, applicants can proceed through the University s postgraduate research application process. Step 8: Explore Funding Opportunities After securing admission, applicants can investigate the University s available postgraduate research scholarships and funding opportunities. Because the University states that scholarship applications are invited once applicants have been accepted onto research degree courses, prospective students should pay close attention to the sequence and deadlines applicable to each funding opportunity. The University of Salford s postgraduate research environment combines independent research with access to academic supervision, research centres and researcher development support. Potential features of the research experience include: Access to the University s Doctoral School . Opportunities to work under academic supervision. Exposure to interdisciplinary research. Access to specialist research centres. Opportunities to develop advanced research skills. Opportunities to build international academic networks. Research opportunities across creative, business, health, scientific and engineering disciplines. Potential access to postgraduate research scholarships and funding. Opportunities to investigate innovative and novel research topics. A research environment connected with real-world social, technological, environmental and economic challenges. The breadth of research specialisms also means that prospective students can explore different academic environments before selecting a research pathway. Visit HERE to learn more about the University of Salford Postgraduate Research Degrees. Important Information for Prospective Applicants Applicants should carefully distinguish between general postgraduate research admission and specific scholarship opportunities . Being eligible to apply for a research degree does not automatically mean that an applicant qualifies for every scholarship offered by the University. Similarly, individual scholarships may have their own requirements concerning nationality, academic background, research topic, funding status or other conditions. Prospective students should therefore: Check the admission requirements for the exact research degree. Review the research interests of potential supervisors. Confirm that their proposed research fits the University s expertise. Check international student requirements if applying from outside the UK. Review current tuition fees. Investigate available scholarships separately. Check individual scholarship deadlines. Prepare application materials well in advance. Contact the relevant postgraduate research team when clarification is required. Deadline No single application deadline is stated in the information provided for University of Salford postgraduate research degrees. Research degree application deadlines can vary according to the specific programme, intake and funding opportunity. Scholarship deadlines may also differ from research degree admission deadlines. Applicants should therefore check the official University of Salford course and funding pages for the latest deadlines applicable to their chosen programme. How to Find Out More and Apply Prospective applicants can explore the University of Salford s postgraduate research programmes through the University s official postgraduate research pages. They can also browse the University s available research degrees, explore research centres and academic profiles, and investigate postgraduate research funding opportunities. Browse Postgraduate Research and Doctoral Degrees Conclusion The University of Salford postgraduate research opportunities provide prospective researchers with access to a wide-ranging research environment in the United Kingdom. From arts, media and creative technologies to business, management and law, health and society, science, engineering and environmental research, the University supports research across numerous academic disciplines. Students can pursue master s-level research qualifications such as the MSc by Research and MPhil , as well as doctoral qualifications including the PhD, DProf and DBA . The University s research centres provide specialised environments for investigating subjects ranging from artificial intelligence, robotics and cybersecurity to sustainable construction, biomedical research, creative technologies, business transformation and international security. The University also provides access to a Doctoral School and offers scholarships and funding opportunities, although scholarship applications are generally invited after applicants have been accepted onto a research degree course. For students seeking advanced research training and the opportunity to contribute original knowledge to their chosen field, Salford s postgraduate research portfolio provides multiple pathways to explore. Applicants should review the requirements of their specific programme, confirm the appropriate application process and check the latest funding and deadline information directly with the University before applying.
